entities.summary: Arakelots Monastery was an Armenian monastery in the historic province of Taron, 11 km south-east of Mush (Muş), in present-day eastern Turkey. According to tradition, Gregory the Illuminator founded the monastery to house relics of several apostles. The monastery was, however, most likely built in the 11th century. During the 12th-13th centuries it was a major center of learning. In the following centuries it was expanded, destroyed and renovated. It remained one of the prominent monasteries of Turkish (Western) Armenia until the Armenian genocide of 1915, when it was attacked and subsequently abandoned.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a major center of learning in medieval West Asia, Arakelots Monastery played a significant role in preserving Armenian culture and knowledge during the 12th-13th centuries. Its historical significance lies in its contribution to the preservation of Christian heritage in the region.
